constraints_found.source_line: maya: "i need pizza. i've been smelling it from the dining hall all morning and i can't take it anymore"

constraints_found.constraint: Preference: fresh and light, not greasy or heavy (Brooke)
constraints_found.source_line: brooke: "just not the greasy, heavy kind for me. something fresh and light"
maya: "fresh is fine. CHEAP is mandatory. one dollar sign max, the trip fund is watching"

constraints_found.constraint: Strict diet: vegetarian (Mina). Picking meat off does not count, so the venue must have real vegetarian pizza
constraints_found.source_line: brooke: "wait, mina, you're vegetarian! you told me in class. picking it off doesn't count" (confirmed by maya: "we are going somewhere with real veggie pizza")

elimination.campus_slice_society: Deal-breaker. Every pizza comes with meat and they won't make one without (review 2). No vegetarian_options tag in the registry. This is the trap: cheap, light and pizza, but Mina can't eat there.
elimination.campus_quad_pizza_co: Pizza, $, has veggie slices, but it is deep, greasy and heavy, so it misses Brooke's fresh and light preference (-1 star, so 2 stars). The registry backs this up: no healthy vibe tag.
elimination.campus_green_bean_cafe: $, healthy, vegetarian, but no pizza ovens, so it misses Maya's pizza craving (-1 star, so 2 stars).
elimination.campus_basil_hearth: Pizza, $, half the menu is veggie, thin and light. Meets every constraint.

notes: The vegetarian trap works well. Mina's 'i can always just pick the pepperoni off' tempts a careless reader to drop the diet, and Brooke shuts that down straight away, so it's fair and still a good catch.

Slice Society's registry tags (peanut_free plus healthy, no vegetarian_options) agree with its review, so a player can spot the trap from either the card or the reviews. That might make it a bit too easy to spot from tags alone, but it is consistent.
Each distractor misses exactly one constraint. That makes the logic clean but fairly easy to solve once all four constraints are listed.
No contradictions found. The trip/coast chatter is harmless flavour.
Minor: Green Bean Cafe is the same price tier and fully healthy/veggie, so a player who forgets the pizza craving might pick it. That's a reasonable secondary distractor.
